site.name: Lady Franklin Mine
site.location: Magnolia Mining District / Eldorado Springs quadrangle
overview: Lady Franklin Mine was a documented gold-and-silver producer in Boulder County's Magnolia Mining District, south of the Gold Hill area.

Historic Boulder County mining literature counted Lady Franklin among the district's principal mines and reported substantial production, while archival newspaper indexing documents active development and management of the property in the early 1880s.

timeline.text: Denver Public Library's Western History Subject Index records McAyeal as a Magnolia mine owner who developed and managed the Lady Franklin Mine, citing Rocky Mountain News items from December 1880 and January 1881.
A published history of Boulder County's gold fields listed Lady Franklin among the principal Magnolia District mines and reported gross production of about $100,000.
USGS-derived Eldorado Springs topographic mapping preserves Lady Franklin Mine as a named Boulder County mine feature.

moreHistory: The Magnolia Mining District was one of Boulder County's important tellurium-gold districts. Historical summaries of the district list Lady Franklin alongside mines such as Keystone, Mountain Lion, Kekionga and Magnolia, placing it within the district's documented producing landscape.

The Boulder County Lady Franklin is distinct from the same-name mine in Custer County. The mapped Boulder County mine-level locality at approximately 39.994431, -105.364993 is used for identification; Remnant does not claim that this point is a field-surveyed surviving shaft or portal.

A focused exact-site media search did not locate a reusable Lady Franklin Mine photograph with sufficiently clear app-use rights. Wrong-site and ambiguous same-name imagery was rejected rather than attached.
